questions.question: What is transport? Name the three ways people travel and give an example of each.
questions.expected_answer: Transport means moving people, animals or goods from one place to another. People travel on land, for example by walking, car, bus or train; on water, for example by canoe, boat or ship; and in the air, for example by balloon, aeroplane or helicopter.

questions.question: How did people move themselves and their goods long ago?
questions.expected_answer: They walked and carried goods on their heads, backs or in their arms. Later they used animals, such as donkeys, horses and oxen, to carry loads and pull sledges, carts and wagons with wheels. On water they used rafts, canoes and sailing boats.

questions.question: Give two ways faster transport has made life better and two problems it has brought.
questions.expected_answer: Better: people can travel further and faster; goods and food can be moved cheaply so trade grows; sick people reach hospitals quickly; families can visit each other. Problems: pollution from exhaust fumes, road accidents, traffic jams, and in South Africa migrant workers were separated from their families.
